extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using the SMPL body model. It contains more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects, more than 11000 motions. The dataset includes SMPL 3D shape parameters, DMPL soft tissue coefficients, and full SMPL pose parameters including hand articulations.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.publisher: MPI for Intelligent Systems, Meshcapade GmbH, York University, MPI for Informatics
extraction.citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278 [cs.CV].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by downloading publicly available mocap datasets from the internet and obtaining several other datasets privately or by recording them directly. The datasets were collected using optical marker-based motion capture systems with varying markersets ranging from 37 to 91 markers. A novel dataset (SSM) was also collected using an OptiTrack motion capture system with 24 Optitrack Prime 17W cameras and 67 reflective markers, synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system capable of capturing high-resolution 3D scans at 60 frames per second.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. A coefficient q is introduced to address missing markers by increasing the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of optical marker-based motion capture data from 15 different datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion Lab, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions. The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. Several datasets were obtained privately or recorded by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: When hand markers are not present on recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ was used to convert mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters (pose, shape, and soft-tissue). The method uses a two-stage optimization: Stage I estimates body shape and marker locations from randomly chosen frames; Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation for each frame. Due to inherent problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and either corrected or held out.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The raw mocap marker data from 15 different datasets with varying markersets was processed using MoSh++ to map all data into a common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameter format. Manual inspection was performed to correct or exclude problematic sequences with swapped and mislabeled markers. Hyperparameters were tuned using cross-validation on the SSM dataset. A weight-balancing factor b=46/n was applied to handle varying numbers of markers across datasets.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (Motion and Shape capture method using SMPL/SMPL-H body model, DMPL soft-tissue model, and MANO hand model); Chumpy autodifferentiation package; Powell's gradient-based dogleg minimization
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape parameters of human subjects. The SSM dataset includes 3D body scans of subjects; two of the three subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: AMASS enables new applications that require large amounts of training data for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning in computer vision. It provides a unified format for human motion data that can be used to train models for human motion understanding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The SSM dataset used for hyperparameter tuning used a standard 46-markerset, which may affect generalization to other markersets. The velocity constancy weights could not be optimized using just one source of data due to dependence on mocap system calibration, optical tracking quality, data frame rate, and types of motions. No ground-truth data is available for evaluating accuracy of hand articulation. Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and testing deep learning models for human motion; animation and visualization; generating synthetic training data for computer vision tasks; modeling human body shape and pose; soft-tissue dynamics modeling; hand articulation capture.
